name: Barnard's Star
description: A nearby red dwarf, 19% of the Sun's width: its disc was measured by interferometry.

radius.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: radius in solar radii, 0.1869 +/- 0.0012, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

mass.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: mass 0.146 solar masses from the K-band mass-luminosity relation of Henry & McCarthy (1993), not a dynamical mass

temperature.source: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 757, 112, Table 6, GJ 699: effective temperature in K, 3222 +/- 10, from the weighted mean of the interferometric measurements the table lists

text.card: A nearby red dwarf whose disc was measured by interferometry: 19% of the Sun's width.
text.introduction: Interferometry gives it 0.1869 solar radii; with its total light, that makes its surface 3,222 K.
